title: Bundy to President Johnson on the Mỹ Cảnh bombing, June 26, 1965 (FRUS 1964–1968, vol. III, doc. 20)
citation: Telegram From the President's Special Assistant for National Security Affairs (Bundy) to President Johnson, in Texas, June 26, 1965, 11:58 a.m. Foreign Relations of the United States, 1964–1968, Volume III, Vietnam, June–December 1965, Document 20 (Washington: Government Printing Office).
notes: The official U.S. record of the Viet Cong bombing of the Mỹ Cảnh floating restaurant on the Saigon River, 25 June 1965, written the next morning. Casualty tally as given: 44 dead (27 Vietnamese, 13 U.S. citizens, 2 French, 1 Swiss, 1 Filipino) and 81 wounded (62 Vietnamese, 16 U.S., 1 Swiss, 2 Germans). Referred to throughout as 'the My Canh atrocity'. Read 2026-09-05 to date the event Larry describes on VN-0068 — being in front of the restaurant when it blew up. The document fixes the date; it says nothing about Larry.
